messages:
acme-customer: We're getting spikes of 429s hitting /v1/generate around our minute-based sync job. Happens for ~6-10s each minute. Sample request id: r-9f4b

lena: Thanks — can you confirm whether those are streaming responses or plain request/response and roughly how many tokens per call?

acme-customer: Plain requests. Inputs ~650 tokens, outputs ~30. We run 18 workers that kick at top of minute with <50ms jitter. Retries are enabled but minimal jitter.

kai: That schedule pattern often creates a concentrated token burst; TPM will eat you before RPM in that case. Do you see Retry-After or rate headers in responses?

acme-customer: Yes, RESP headers show 429 and some x-tpm-* headers but they're noisy. We'll paste one here after next run.

devx_jay: Immediate customer guidance:
- distribute start times (even +/- seconds) across workers
- use full jitter in backoff (https://www.awsarchitectureblog.com/2015/03/backoff.html)
- if possible, break large inputs into streamed chunks so token emission is paced
- consider a small pre-warming phase to smooth bursts (eg. staggered warmup requests)

ops_oncall: Internal checklist:
- query per-tenant token-rate timeseries for last 60m
- confirm whether gateway aggregated tokens incorrectly for multiplexed connections
- review proxy logs for client retry amplification

lena: Please run this curl from one worker during the next sync window and paste headers so we confirm quota fields:

curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-standard","input":"<sample>"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

acme-customer: Pasted response from :00 run:
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-request-id: r-9f4b
x-rpm-limit: 1200
x-rpm-remaining: 2
x-tpm-limit: 90000
x-tpm-remaining: 0

kai: That nails TPM exhaustion. Note x-rpm-remaining looking okay because the short window compresses RPM but token volume kills TPM.

devx_jay: Short-term ops options: authorize a temporary TPM uplift for 12-24h while they roll out staggers; or enable a soft-queue at the edge that returns Retry-After instead of immediate 429 (requires SRE review).

sales_amy: I can approve a 24h token uplift if they provide a mitigation timeline and runbook. Send account id and ETA.

acme-customer: We'll implement staggered start + full jitter in next 15 minutes and report back with headers.

ops_oncall: Created INC-2026-2048 to track. Assigned to eng-sre for edge-queue feasibility. TTL for uplift: 24h. Monitor dashboards for the next 2 cycles.

lena: Thanks all. @acme-customer once you post the after-change headers we'll validate TPM consumption dropped and close the uplift.

acme-customer: Post-change headers (after stagger):
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-request-id: r-9f4b
x-rpm-limit: 1200
x-rpm-remaining: 1180
x-tpm-limit: 90000
x-tpm-remaining: 81500

kai: Looks good — tokens/min now within limits. Closing action: verify steady-state over next 24h and document for quota guidance. :white_check_mark:
